classification.difficultyReason: Link midpoint and distance calculations, then recognise a parallelogram from two equal pairs of opposite sides; repeated calculations add little additional conceptual demand.

content.prompt: The quadrilateral $ABCD$ has vertices $A(1,0)$, $B(4,8)$, $C(11,12)$ and $D(-1,10)$. $M$, $N$, $O$ and $P$ are the midpoints of the sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$ respectively. Find the lengths of the sides of quadrilateral $MNOP$ and describe this quadrilateral.

inlines.text: MNOP is a parallelogram because both pairs of opposite sides are equal.

answer.worked:
Using the midpoint formula,
$$\begin{align*}
M&=\left(\frac{1+4}{2},\frac{0+8}{2}\right)=\left(\frac52,4\right)\\
N&=\left(\frac{4+11}{2},\frac{8+12}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{15}2,10\right)\\
O&=\left(\frac{11+(-1)}2,\frac{12+10}2\right)=(5,11)\\
P&=\left(\frac{-1+1}2,\frac{10+0}2\right)=(0,5).
\end{align*}$$
Using the distance formula,
$$\begin{align*}
MN^2&=\left(\frac{15}2-\frac52\right)^2+(10-4)^2\\
MN^2&=25+36=61\\
MN&=\sqrt{61}\\
NO^2&=\left(5-\frac{15}2\right)^2+(11-10)^2\\
NO^2&=\frac{25}4+1=\frac{29}4\\
NO&=\frac{\sqrt{29}}2\\
OP^2&=(0-5)^2+(5-11)^2\\
OP^2&=25+36=61\\
OP&=\sqrt{61}\\
PM^2&=\left(\frac52-0\right)^2+(4-5)^2\\
PM^2&=\frac{25}4+1=\frac{29}4\\
PM&=\frac{\sqrt{29}}2.
\end{align*}$$
Both pairs of opposite sides are equal, so $MNOP$ is a parallelogram.
